result.answer:
Yes. Cloudflare’s status page reports a recent incident that specifically involves cache purging:

| Incident ID | Title | Status | Affected Component | Relevant Update |
|-------------|-------|--------|--------------------|-----------------|
| **wp49bp8bqo6c** | Fedramp Customers have Delayed Purges | *identified* | CDN Cache Purge | “Cloudflare has identified a bug with our purge pipeline impacting fedramp customers. Stale content may be served until expired. Non‑fedramp customers are **not impacted**.” |

- The incident was first posted on 2026‑11‑06 17:47 UTC and is still *identified* (no resolution yet).  
- The update explicitly states that only FedRAMP customers are affected, while non‑FedRAMP customers are not impacted.

**Answer to your questions**

1. **Cloudflare cache purge incident** – Yes, there was an incident (ID wp49bp8bqo6c) that directly involved the CDN cache‑purge pipeline.  
2. **Effect on a non‑FedRAMP website** – According to the incident’s updates, a website that is *not* a FedRAMP customer should **not** have been affected by this bug.  

**Evidence URL**  
[https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/wp49bp8bqo6c](https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/wp49bp8bqo6c)

result.answer:
**GitHub Incident xr3myzj7ms51 – “Incident with Actions and Pages”**

- **Affected components** (as listed in the incident record):  
  • Webhooks  
  • Actions  
  • Pages  
  • Code Scanning  
  • Copilot coding agent  

- **Relation to Actions**:  
  The incident explicitly states that *GitHub Actions* experienced significant delays. Actions workflow runs and job‑status updates were delayed by up to **25 minutes** during the affected periods. Therefore, Actions is one of the components that were impacted.

**Source**

updates.body:
On November 4, 2026, between 15:49 UTC and 16:48 UTC, and again between 17:20 UTC and 17:55 UTC, GitHub Actions, Pages, Webhooks, Code Scanning, and Copilot coding agent experienced delays. During this time, Actions workflow runs and job status updates were delayed by up to 25 minutes. Pages deployments dropped to about 4% of normal volume, webhook deliveries dropped to about 58% of normal volume, and Code Scanning analyses and Copilot coding agent sessions were delayed. Delayed events were processed after mitigation.

This incident was caused by a configuration change to an internal event-routing service that unexpectedly paused delivery of several event streams. The change depended on feature flags that were not set up as intended, which the service did not handle gracefully. We mitigated the first period by rolling back the configuration change at 16:14 UTC. The code change
The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability.
We are investigating reports of degraded performance for Actions and Pages

If you need a definitive list of all incidents that occurred in 2025, you would need to use a service that archives the full incident history (e.g., GitHub’s own incident database or a third‑party monitoring service) or manually review the GitHub Status page’s archive for that year.

On November 4, 2026, between 15:49 UTC and 16:48 UTC, and again between 17:20 UTC and 17:55 UTC, GitHub Actions, Pages, Webhooks, Code Scanning, and Copilot coding agent experienced delays. During this time, Actions workflow runs and job status updates were delayed by up to 25 minutes. Pages deployments dropped to about 4% of normal volume, webhook deliveries dropped to about 58% of normal volume, and Code Scanning analyses and Copilot coding agent sessions were delayed. Delayed events were processed after mitigation.

This incident was caused by a configuration change to an internal event-routing service that unexpectedly paused delivery of several event streams.
